title: Operations, Research, and Broad Innovative Technology Services (ORBIT) Request for Information (RFI) and Sources Sought Notice (SSN)
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC) Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) is hereby solicitating information from potential sources for the Operations, Research, and Broad Innovative Technology Services (ORBIT) solicitation. NASA JSC is issuing this RFI/SSN as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in, and the resources to support this requirement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the type and method of procurement. A draft Statement of Work (dSOW) is in the attachment section for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to verify reasonableness and feasibility of the requirement, as well as promote competition. NASA JSC is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of Small Businesses (SB) and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals for ORBIT. Vendors are encouraged to demonstrate capabilities as a prime, subcontractor and/or teaming partner. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), HUBZone, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) business set-aside based on responses received. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: 1. SB Subcontracting goals; 2. Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or 3. Strategies to increase SB participation, including: � Breaking requirements into smaller components � Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting � Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, and the corresponding small business size standard is $34 million, calculated in accordance with 13 CFR 121.104. ORBIT Description: The proposed ORBIT contract will provide mission engineering, spaceflight-enabling, mission support, and advanced technology services to NASA's Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) at Johnson Space Center (JSC) and its mission partners. It is anticipated that the ORBIT will be a multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle with Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task orders. This acquisition will establish a follow-on contract vehicle to succeed the Mission Enabling Support Contract MESC-IDIQ contracts, encompassing the legacy and a subset of those requirements including partial scope of MESC-B, which are scheduled to expire on September 30, 2027. The follow- on contract restructures the acquisition strategy to better align functionally related capability areas as part of a single procurement , reduces the contract administration burden on the Government, improves small business participation and competition at the task order level, and provides a more efficient and flexible contracting mechanism for the delivery of the following Functional Area Requirements identified in the dSOW: � Functional Area 1 - Mission and Systems Engineering Support � Functional Area 2 - Technical Evaluation, Analysis, and Independent Assessment � Functional Area 3 Specialized IT and Operations � Functional Area 4 - Advanced Mission R&D No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. Interested firms are responsible for monitoring this website for the release of any solicitation or synopsis. Interested firms having the required capabilities necessary to meet the above requirement described herein should submit a capability statement of no more than 10 pages indicating the ability to perform all aspects of the effort. Capability Statement: Interested firms having the required capabilities necessary to meet the above requirement should indicate the ability to perform all aspects of the effort, and include the following information: 1. Technical - Describe your company's overall skills, experience, and capabilities to perform the work of the ORBIT dSOW. Please identify specific dSOW sections where your company could provide the stated capability by way of Attachment 1 - Vendor Capability Matrix at the end of this announcement. If subcontracting or if a joint venture is anticipated, organizations should address the anticipated administrative and management structure of such arrangements (if this information is known at this time). Also address what elements of work would be performed by the prime or joint venture partners and which elements would be performed by subcontractors. 2. General � a. What additional documents would you like to see on the ORBIT contract website or included in the Technical Library? b. What barriers or obstacles do you foresee to potentially bidding on this contract? Can you identify any Government acquisition approaches that would increase the competitiveness of this procurement? What innovations might you propose in the performance of this contract or contract structure? c. What innovations might you propose in the performance of this contract or contract structure? 3. Company-Specific Information - Responses must include the following: a. Company�s name, address, and a point of contact (name, e-mail address, and address) b. Unique Entity Identifier number and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code c. Number of years in business d. Size of business i. Average annual revenue for past three years ii. Number of employees iii. Whether the firm is a Large, SB, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), HUBZone, WOSB, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), SDVOSB, HBCU/MI, and/or 8a e. Ownership, affiliate information (as applicable) including parent company and joint venture partners f. If you plan to propose as a prime or as a subcontractor; g. A list of contracts covering the past three years with emphasis on work performed for the United States Federal Government. Please provide contract numbers, if your firm was a prime or subcontractor, contract type, dollar value of each procurement, and customer point of contact (address, phone, and email). If work was performed as a subcontractor, please indicate percentage of work/subcontract dollar value. If the contract(s) were IDIQ, please indicate the number of task orders awarded and the total dollar value of those task orders. h. Company�s specific capabilities that are relevant to the requirements contemplated above. It is not sufficient to provide general brochures or generic information. This RFI/SSN is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Respondents deemed fully qualified will be considered in any resultant solicitation for the requirement. All responses must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer at jsc-orbit-procurement@mail.nasa.gov no later than 5:00 PM CENTRAL DAYLIGHT TIME on October 05, 2026. Please reference �ORBIT Sources Sought� in the subject line of any response. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurem

title: GSA PBS Large Construction IDIQ
description: This is a REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI). Place of Performance: The 50 States of the United States of America and U.S. Territories NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction The U.S. General Services Administration, Public Buildings Service (GSA PBS) is seeking information regarding the below potential requirement. Firms that are considered either a small business or other than small business under NAICS code 236220 may submit a response to this RFI. This RFI is issued solely for planning purposes. It is not a Request for Proposals, and there is no bid package or solicitation document associated with this RFI. The requested information does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that a procurement action will be issued. The Government shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for proprietary information not properly identified. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Responses to this RFI are not offers, and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No contract will be awarded from this announcement. This is not an announcement of a forthcoming solicitation, nor is it a request seeking contractors to be placed on a mailing list. Data submitted in response to this RFI will not be returned, and those who respond to this RFI should not anticipate feedback regarding any submission. The Government reserves the right to determine how to proceed as a result of this RFI. GSA PBS seeks comments and suggestions that may be used in planning support of potential requirements. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI is strictly voluntary and at no cost to the Government. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. GSA PBS is contemplating a solicitation for General Construction with Design Build and Construction Manager as Constructor (CMc) capabilities and is seeking information about contractors� ability to provide timely, cost-effective, and quality general construction services with the optimum geographic coverage for numerous states. The anticipated multiple award Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts would service geographic locations within the 50 States of the United States of America and the U.S. Territories. IDIQ contracts would be awarded by pre-established zones. The Government shall endeavor to utilize this contract to the maximum practical extent. However, the Government reserves the right to perform, or have performed by others, any services required, and doing so shall not breach or otherwise violate this contract. These IDIQ contracts would have a period of performance of at least five years, with 1 five-year base period and 5 one-year option periods for a potential 10-year period of performance. GSA PBS anticipates awarding multiple IDIQ contracts (potentially 40-50), and the cumulative maximum ordering limitation (MOL) is currently being determined. The total MOL will be available at award to be utilized over 10 years if all options are exercised. Typical task orders would range from $20,000,000 and up, however task orders could be awarded at amounts under $20,000,000. GSA anticipates that the IDIQ contracts would include the ability for contractor on/off-ramping as-needed during the period of performance. GSA PBS is considering using a self-scoring scorecard to evaluate offerors' technical capabilities, past performance and experience. It is anticipated that offerors would submit one scorecard per proposed zone, up to a maximum of 7 scorecards, and must provide supporting documentation for each claimed point. Following solicitation closing, the Government anticipates validating all claimed scoring elements. It is anticipated that IDIQ contracts will be awarded to the highest technically rated offerors in each zone with fair and reasonable pricing. A sample scorecard is attached to this RFI. Task orders will be competed among all contractors in their primary zone, however the Task Order CO reserves the right to compete a Task Order across multiple Zones; however the primary zone will always be competed . GSA anticipates these IDIQ contracts will provide the capability for other Federal agencies (in addition to GSA) to directly place task orders against the IDIQs.The zones will be as follows: Zones Zone 1 Maryland, Virginia, Washington DC Zone 2 Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont Zone 3 Alabama, Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands Zone 4 Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Tennessee, West Virginia, Wisconsin Zone 5 Arkansas, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, Wyoming Zone 6 Louisiana, Mississippi, Texas Zone 7 Alaska, Arizona, California, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, American Samoa, Guam, Northern Marianas, Saipan For the IDIQ price evaluation, GSA anticipates that each offeror will propose a percentage rate to be used as the Profit Rate for each task order proposal. The rate will be applied to the task order summary proposal subtotal. For task order proposals, an offeror may use a profit rate lower than their pre-negotiated profit rate, but not higher. However, for any project for which competition is opened to one or more secondary zones, the pre-negotiated rate is not required for that project, for any offeror under that TO RFP. This rate will remain unchanged throughout the life of the contract, including any extensions, and will apply to the initial task order award and all modifications for projects solicited to only the contractors in the primary zone. The rate which is used in the initial negotiation and award of a task order will continue to be used for all modifications to that task order. The Government anticipates that task orders over the threshold for large-scale construction projects (currently $35 million) would require a Project Labor Agreement (PLA) unless an exception is approved. The Government is considering structuring the IDIQ contracts to provide order-level flexibility for task orders to be placed that are either commercial or non-commercial. If interested in responding to this RFI, please respond by completing and submitting the GSA PBS Large Construction IDIQ RFI Questionnaire no later than 5:00pm Central Standard Time on Monday, October 5, 2026. The form must be completed no later than 5:00pm, Monday, October 5, 2026. All prospective responders are responsible for monitoring this site for the release of all other information pertaining to the RFI and future sources sought or solicitation, if any. NO TELEPHONE CALLS WILL BE ACCEPTED. Attachments: Proposed Zonal Maps PBS Nationwide Large Construction IDIQ Scorecard

Szczegółowy zakres usług ujęty w załączonym Przedmiarze robót oraz Specyfikacji Technicznej. 9. Wykonawca zobowiązuje się do zawarcia na własny koszt odpowiednich umów ubezpieczenia z tytułu odpowiedzialności cywilnej na czas realizacji zamówienia. 10. Ubezpieczeniu podlega odpowiedzialność cywilna kontraktowa oraz deliktowa za szkody oraz następstwa nieszczęśliwych wypadków dotyczące pracowników i osób trzecich, powstałe w związku z prowadzonymi usługami - wymagana suma ubezpieczenia nie mniej niż 50 tys. zł na jedno zdarzenie. 11. Kopie polis lub dokumentów ubezpieczeniowych potwierdzone za zgodność z oryginałem, Wykonawca przedłoży do wglądu Zamawiającemu najpóźniej w dniu przekazania miejsca wykonania zamówienia i następnie na każde żądanie Zamawiającego. Opóźnienie z tego tytułu będzie traktowane, jako powstałe z przyczyn zależnych od wykonawcy i nie może stanowić podstawy do zmiany terminu zakończenia zamówienia. 12. Zamawiający stosownie do art. 95 ust. 1 ustawy Pzp, wymaga zatrudnienia przez wykonawcę lub podwykonawcę na podstawie umowy o pracę osób wykonujących czynności: kierowcy sprzętu transportowego, operatorzy sprzętu, osoby sprzątające nawierzchnię w zakresie realizacji zamówienia 13. Zamawiający dopuszcza możliwości składania ofert częściowych zgodnie z opisem przedmiotu zamówienia. 14. Istnieje możliwość unieważnienia postępowania w następstwie nieprzyznania środków na sfinansowanie zamówienia. Zgodnie z art. 257 ustawy Pzp Zamawiający może unieważnić postępowanie o udzielenie zamówienia, jeżeli środki Publiczne, które zamawiający zamierzał przeznaczyć na sfinansowanie całości lub części zamówienia, nie zostały mu przyznane, a możliwość unieważnienia postępowania na tej podstawie została przewidziana w ogłoszeniu zamówienia.

title: GB-London: Consultancy Required for LondonEnergy Future Transport Yard Feasibility
description: LEL must establish whether the Hawley Road site can be retained or, if not, identify a suitable replacement capable of meeting current and future operational requirements before the lease expires in February 2030. The key question is what constitutes the most deliverable, operationally suitable and value-for-money solution for providing LEL's transport yard facilities beyond February 2030. LEL will therefore appoint a suitably qualified consultant to undertake a feasibility study and strategic options appraisal, assessing suitable alternatives and recommending a preferred option and next steps. Based on LEL's estimated timescales for designing, constructing and transitioning into a new site, there is a need to undertake a feasibility study to identify alternative transport yard options as soon as possible, with a preferred way forward decided by June 2027. This timetable is intended to enable the preferred option to progress into design and procurement during 2027, followed by the necessary environmental assessment, planning and permitting activities and subject to approvals, construction. The Consultant shall therefore plan and deliver the commission to support timely decision-making and protect the overall programme ahead of the Hawley Road lease expiry in February 2030. Additional information: The contracting authority considers that this contract may be suitable for economic operators that are small or medium enterprises (SMEs). However, any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement.

title: Request for Information 3- Next Generation of the GSA SmartPay� Master Contract
description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION IS SOLELY FOR INFORMATIONAL AND PLANNING PURPOSES AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. Responses to this RFI do not constitute an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested and/or received in response to the request. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. Information received in response to this RFI will be safeguarded adequately from unauthorized disclosure. Proprietary information should be clearly marked. Purpose and Introduction The General Services Administration (GSA) Payment Solutions Service Center (PSSC) is responsible for overall program management and leadership of the GSA SmartPay� program. This government-wide program and awarded master contracts currently provides commercial charge card and payment related services to approximately 250 federal government agencies, certain eligible organizations, and Native American Tribal organizations. In fiscal year (FY) 2025, approximately 4.2 million GSA SmartPay 3 card/account holders spent nearly $40 billion, through 82 million transactions. The current period of performance for the GSA SmartPay 3 master contract ends November 29, 2031, if all options are exercised. Since 2024, PSSC has been conducting market research and acquisition planning for the next iteration of the GSA SmartPay master contract. PSSC has actively engaged GSA SmartPay customers, current GSA SmartPay master contract awardees and partners, and prospective new industry providers. The goal of this acquisition is to develop a program that is responsive to the unique needs of GSA SmartPay customers, while encouraging participation from both traditional financial institutions and innovative new entrants. Through market research activities, PSSC collected customer feedback about the GSA SmartPay 3 master contract and program that includes the following: Concerns about charge card management system functionality Desire to leverage commercial innovation while balancing aging systems and government policies and regulations Need for prospective offers with the appropriate financial capabilities and fundamentals to support government operations and needs Need for more flexibility and control over agency or organization-specific requirements for their programs and task orders Conclusions from industry feedback about the GSA SmartPay 3 master contract and program include: Both traditional financial institutions and innovative new entrants are likely able to support the scope of services for the GSA SmartPay program There are barriers to entry, which are based in aligning the next program with commercial practices and include the following: Pricing structure and period of performance Non-commercial requirements Stringent security requirements As such, for the development of the next iteration of the GSA SmartPay program/contract(s), PSSC has focused on three themes: Commerciality Innovation Security PSSC is seeking feedback from both GSA SmartPay customers and the commercial payments industry for the draft Pricing (Section B) and Performance Work Statement (PWS) (Section C) (Attachment 1). The intention of the drafts is to ensure that GSA SmartPay customers benefit from ongoing commercial payments innovation while meeting the mission critical and government-specific needs. At the same time, the draft pricing and PWS focuses on leveraging existing and emerging secure commercial functionality and processes to reduce barriers for entry for prospective offerors. Submission of Feedback/Comments Interested parties are invited to submit all feedback/comments regarding the Draft GSA SmartPay 4 Pricing and Performance Work Statement (PWS) in the attached Excel response template (Attachment 2 - Feedback Template) format via email to SPcard@gsa.gov and jennifer.g.richards@gsa.gov. The email subject line shall include the text "PWS Feedback: RFI 47QRAB26N0003�. Emails without this text in the subject line may not be acknowledged. Do not submit responses in the text of an email. Submission of a general statement of capability or company profile is acceptable for informational purposes. Responses that fail to follow the required format may be excluded from consideration or review. This RFI is being conducted for market research purposes only. A company�s decision to submit or not submit a response, and/or the extent of the government�s review/consideration of any submitted response, will have no impact on a contractor's ability to compete for any future requirements that may follow this RFI. title: „Praha, MO Valy –centrální registr MO – rozšíření a rekonstrukce“
description: 1. Etapa: zpracování dokumentace pro vydání povolení záměru stavby, projednání s dotčenými orgány, zabezpečení pravomocného povolení záměru Stavby. 2. Etapa: zpracování dokumentace pro provádění Stavby, zpracování výkazu výměr, kontrolního rozpočtu, harmonogramu projekčních prací a Příručky pro užívání a údržbu dokončeného díla - Operational & Maintenance Manual, zajištění osoby koordinátora BOZP na staveništi a vypracování Plánu BOZP na staveništi. 3. Etapa: zajištění dozoru projektanta. Nad rámec činností specifikovaných v sazebníku UNIKA je požadována účast na všech kontrolních jednáních o výstavbě. Dále je požadováno zabezpečení Dozoru projektanta při případném dopracování realizační dílenské dokumentace Stavby (Zhotovitelem Stavby) s vysvětlením příslušných vazeb, popř. s koordinační působností mezi jednotlivými zpracovateli 4. Etapa: zajištění osoby Koordinátora BOZP, bude-li prokázána nutnost takové činnosti v době realizace Stavby. 5. Etapa: Zajištění řádného výkonu činnosti technického dozoru stavebníka a provádění činnosti TDS kvalifikovanými osobami s příslušnou odbornou způsobilostí, bude-li prokázána nutnost takové činnosti v době realizace Stavby. Jedná se o rozšíření a rekonstrukce kancelářských prostor na technické místnosti s nepřetržitým provozem a stálou směnou, realizací Stavby pak vzniknou zabezpečené prostory k implementaci nových utajovaných informačních systémů, rozšíření a výměnu zastaralých bezpečnostních prvků k zajištění utajovaných informací kategorie „Přísně tajné“ v režimu zvláštního přístupu na adrese Tychonova 1, 160 01 Praha 6 – Hradčany, budova č. 7.
